fact: The Minister for Finance's 2026/27 budget speech commits PMO-RALG with TRA to complete TAUSI-IDRAS integration, add a TAUSI module for registering, identifying and taking payments on buildings by use, and add a module letting street and village executives register all traders.

The speech assigns the TAUSI system, on which traders apply for business licences and upload TRA tax clearance certificates, to the Prime Minister's Office - Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG) for development.
The Controller and Auditor General's audit of FY2024/25 lists TAUSI as a revenue system managed by PMO-RALG as a centrally hosted application used by user public entities.
The audit records that PMO-RALG manages the TAUSI revenue system.

The Controller and Auditor General reviewed bills issued through the TAUSI system to 30 June 2025 and found TZS 1.22 billion issued by seven LGAs unpaid, and cites the revenue administration manual requiring system bills to update taxpayer records on payment.

PMO-RALG instructed LGAs on 31 January 2023 to install TAUSI by 31 March 2023 and stop collecting on LGRCIS; the audit draws TAUSI collection reports for 184 LGAs' own-source revenue (TZS 1.46 trillion in 2024/25) through PMO-RALG.
PMO-RALG operates TAUSI, adding a TAUSI module for property management under the mandate from January 2024 that moved property rates to LGAs.

At Dar es Salaam City Council, agents collected TZS 1.01 billion of solid waste fees on point-of-sale machines through the discontinued LGRCIS in 2024/25, of which TZS 742.29 million had been banked by 21 October 2025.

The brief reports that Tanzania's Public Finance Management Reform Program, led by the Ministry of Finance and Planning, counts the launch of LGRCIS (with GePG) among its achievements, a simplification of non-tax revenue collection.
The Chanzo, citing the CAG report for 2023/24, says 16 councils collected TZS 6.68 billion through the old LGRCIS instead of TAUSI; no total of councils is given.
A PO-RALG (TAMISEMI) assistant director said on 10 September 2025 that collecting with the old system breached government directives to use TAUSI, which the ministry directs.

The PO-RALG official said some councils issue receipts that do not come from the system, mostly on produce sources using POS machines, which shows TAUSI's receipts and POS devices are the record; the old system had no tracking of staff collections.
PO-RALG directive of 31 January 2023 told local government authorities to install TAUSI by 31 March 2023, register all POS devices and stop collecting through LGRCIS.
The CAG says there is no budget for system implementation in 137 LGAs and recommends PO-RALG secure funding for the full rollout of TAUSI in all 184 LGAs.

The audit reviewed bills issued through TAUSI by LGAs for the period ended 30 June 2024; the Revenue Administration Manual it cites says taxpayer records in the billing system update automatically on payment.
The CAG says the system is designed with taxpayer databases, e-receipts and reports; it lists TZS 12.20 billion of defaulters held in LGRCIS across 26 LGAs, so LGRCIS held debtors against payers.

The CAG found 16 LGAs collected TZS 6.68 billion through LGRCIS instead of TAUSI in 2023/24 because sources such as hotel levy and building permits were not configured in TAUSI; no total is stated here.
Table 20 lists 20 LGAs with revenue collected through TAUSI but not banked in 2023/24, and 23 with LGRCIS; the count of LGAs using TAUSI is a floor.
PO-RALG implemented the TAUSI property tax module in only 47 of 184 LGAs (25.5 percent, computed from the CAG's 47 and 137), the rest relying on TANESCO collections; December 2024 reporting.
PO-RALG's minister told the National Assembly that by February 2023, 169 councils had started to use TAUSI, which replaced LGRCIS in 2022/23; no total of councils is given in this document.
PO-RALG built TAUSI to fix problems of LGRCIS, in use from the 2022/23 financial year, with USAID PS3+ support to the revenue system.

The IEG review says LGRCIS automates billing through bar codes on invoices, and by project closure taxpayers in all project cities had electronic bills and electronic receipts; before the project billing and receipts were manual.
LGRCIS was developed under the Strategic Cities Project for its 8 participating LGAs, closing 26 November 2020, where taxpayers had electronic bills and receipts.
The ICR as reported by IEG says LGRCIS was scaled up from 8 LGAs to all 185 LGAs in mainland Tanzania; the review states no use or date for the 185, so the document's publication date applies.
LGRCIS was developed under the World Bank-financed Strategic Cities Project (IDA credits, total cost USD 340.4 million) implemented through PO-RALG.
